title: The Fornax Cluster VLT Spectroscopic Survey - V. Mass modelling of the BCG NGC 1399 out to 150 kpc
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. 23 pages, 20 figures, including a 7-page appendix with 8 figures
summary: NGC 1399, the bright central galaxy of the Fornax cluster, hosts an extensive population of globular clusters (GCs) extending beyond 200 kpc into its outer halo, about 6.5 effective radii (Re). We conducted dynamical mass modelling of NGC 1399 out to 5 Re (~150 kpc), using a comprehensive radial velocity catalogue of GCs, combining data from the Fornax cluster VLT spectroscopic survey (FVSS) with prior measurements from the literature. Applying spherical Jeans equations, we performed dispersion-kurtosis modelling of NGC 1399's GC kinematics to derive its mass profile and GC orbital anisotropy. We also investigated the impact of including intra-cluster GCs in the mass modelling, selected based on spatial segregation and a velocity $σ$-clipping method. Our findings indicate that both cusp-like (NFW) and core-like (Burkert) halos can reproduce the observed kinematics of GCs. Including the intra-cluster GCs in the mass modelling yields broadly consistent mass profiles for both halo types, with the full GC sample giving a virial mass of log $\log M_{\rm vir} = 13.81 \pm 0.09~M_{\odot}$ for the NFW halo, slightly higher than the value inferred for the Burkert halo. Regardless of the dark matter halo profile adopted, we observe that the intra-cluster GCs exhibit radial anisotropy in the outskirts, especially among the blue, metal-poor GCs. These results suggest that GCs in NGC 1399's outer halo are influenced by an additional halo component associated with the galaxy cluster potential. The radial anisotropy observed in these outer-halo GCs provides strong dynamical evidence supporting their accretion from external sources, consistent with prior photometric and spectroscopic studies of GCs. This study highlights the importance of including intra-cluster GCs in dynamical mass modelling to fully account for the contribution of dark matter to the cluster gravitational potential.

AI.tldr: The paper presents dynamical mass modelling of NGC 1399, the central galaxy of the Fornax cluster, out to ~5 Re (~150 kpc) using Jeans dispersion-kurtosis modelling of globular cluster (GC) kinematics from the Fornax VLT spectroscopic survey and literature data. Both NFW and Burkert dark matter halos fit the data, with a virial mass of log M_vir = 13.81 ± 0.09 M☉ for NFW. Intra-cluster GCs show radial anisotropy in the outskirts, especially among blue/metal-poor GCs, providing dynamical evidence for external accretion of these outer GCs and highlighting the importance of including intra-cluster GCs in mass modelling.
AI.motivation: To derive the mass profile and GC orbital anisotropy of NGC 1399 out to 5 Re using GC kinematics, and to assess the impact of including intra-cluster GCs on the dynamical mass modelling to fully account for dark matter contributions to the cluster gravitational potential.
AI.method: Spherical Jeans equations were applied for dispersion-kurtosis modelling of GC kinematics from a combined radial velocity catalogue (FVSS + literature). Intra-cluster GCs were identified via spatial segregation and velocity σ-clipping, and their inclusion in the mass modelling was tested. Both cuspy (NFW) and core-like (Burkert) dark matter halo profiles were fit.
AI.result: Both NFW and Burkert halos reproduce the observed GC kinematics. Including intra-cluster GCs yields broadly consistent mass profiles for both halo types; the full GC sample gives log M_vir = 13.81 ± 0.09 M☉ for NFW, slightly higher than for Burkert. Intra-cluster GCs (especially blue, metal-poor ones) exhibit radial anisotropy in the outskirts.
AI.conclusion: The radial anisotropy of outer-halo GCs provides strong dynamical evidence for their accretion from external sources, consistent with prior photometric and spectroscopic studies. The study emphasizes that including intra-cluster GCs in dynamical mass modelling is crucial to fully account for dark matter in the cluster gravitational potential.

title: Galaxy-LRD Strong Lenses: A Missing Population?
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures. To be submitted to ApJL
summary: The physical nature of Little Red Dots (LRDs) remains uncertain, although these abundant, compact, and red sources may offer important insights into early black-hole growth and galaxy formation. Strong gravitational lensing can magnify LRDs and spatially resolve their internal structure, thereby helping to discriminate among competing physical scenarios. However, no galaxy-scale strongly lensed LRD has yet been securely confirmed. To predict the abundance of such systems in current and future surveys and to guide dedicated searches, we present the first benchmark estimate of the detectable population of galaxy-scale lensed LRDs by combining literature-based LRD source models with a population of foreground early-type galaxy deflectors. Our Monte Carlo simulation spans $50~{\rm deg}^{2}$ and contains 270,713 LRDs and 5,460,841 deflectors. We predict idealized surface densities of $10.70\pm3.76~{\rm deg}^{-2}$ for doubles and $0.64\pm0.69~{\rm deg}^{-2}$ for quads. After accounting for the JWST point-spread function and survey limiting magnitudes, the detectable surface densities decrease to $3.70\pm1.89~{\rm deg}^{-2}$ and $0.52\pm0.58~{\rm deg}^{-2}$, respectively. For the de-duplicated $0.66~{\rm deg}^{2}$ footprint covered by COSMOS-Web, PRIMER-UDS, PRIMER-COSMOS, CEERS, JADES GOODS-S, and JADES GOODS-N, for which the reported limiting depths are combined through area-weighted averaging in flux space, the predicted probabilities of detecting no systems are $8.6\%$ for doubles and $70.8\%$ for quads.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the first benchmark estimate of the detectable population of galaxy-scale strongly lensed Little Red Dots (LRDs) by combining literature-based LRD source models with foreground early-type galaxy deflectors in a Monte Carlo simulation spanning 50 deg².
AI.motivation: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are abundant, compact, red sources whose physical nature is uncertain. Strong gravitational lensing could magnify and spatially resolve their internal structure to discriminate among competing physical scenarios, yet no galaxy-scale strongly lensed LRD has been securely confirmed. A benchmark prediction of the detectable lensed LRD population is needed to guide dedicated searches.
AI.method: A Monte Carlo simulation covering 50 deg² combines literature-based LRD source models with a population of foreground early-type galaxy deflectors, generating 270,713 LRDs and 5,460,841 deflectors. Detectable surface densities are estimated after accounting for the JWST point-spread function and survey limiting magnitudes, with predicted detection probabilities computed for specific survey footprints using area-weighted averaging in flux space.
AI.result: Idealized surface densities are predicted at 10.70±3.76 deg⁻² for doubles and 0.64±0.69 deg⁻² for quads. After JWST PSF and magnitude-limit corrections, detectable densities drop to 3.70±1.89 deg⁻² (doubles) and 0.52±0.58 deg⁻² (quads). For the 0.66 deg² de-duplicated COSMOS-Web/PRIMER/CEERS/JADES footprint, the probability of detecting no systems is 8.6% for doubles and 70.8% for quads.
AI.conclusion: Galaxy-scale strongly lensed LRDs should be detectable in current JWST surveys, particularly doubles, though quads remain rare. The predictions provide quantitative guidance for dedicated lensed-LRD searches and suggest that non-detection of doubles across the combined survey footprint is unlikely (~8.6% chance).

title: Cloud Scale Star Formation and Gas Scaling Relations in the Milky Way
comment: 15 pages, 10 figures, Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We investigate cloud-scale star formation in the Milky Way using a sample of 45 molecular clouds (sizes of $5-240$ pc) in the inner Galactic plane, spanning heliocentric distances of $1.1-14.4$ kpc. Masses of these clouds are derived from $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO emission, while stellar masses are estimated using the young stellar object (YSO) population. The studied molecular clouds have masses ranging from $\sim10^{3}$ to $2.3\times10^{6}$ $\rm M_\odot$, with star formation efficiencies (SFE) up to 0.33. We find a tight, nearly linear scaling of the star formation rate (SFR) with the cloud mass, indicating that more massive clouds form proportionally more stars. The SFE, however, shows a declining trend with cloud mass. The relation between the star formation rate surface density ($Σ_{\rm SFR}$) and gas surface density ($Σ_{\rm gas}$) exhibits substantial cloud-to-cloud scatter, indicating that the canonical Kennicutt--Schmidt law is not strongly recovered at the scale of individual molecular clouds. Incorporating the cloud free-fall time ($\rm t_{ff}$) into the star formation scaling relation highlights its important role in regulating star formation, although the observed relations suggest that the star formation efficiency per free-fall time is not universal. In particular, the SFE decreases with increasing gas mass available per free-fall time. We discuss the implications of our results in the context of recent theoretical models of molecular cloud evolution and star formation.

AI.tldr: Using 45 molecular clouds in the inner Galactic plane, this study finds that the star formation rate scales nearly linearly with cloud mass, but the star formation efficiency declines with increasing cloud mass and per free-fall time, questioning the universality of the Kennicutt-Schmidt law and SFE per free-fall time at the cloud scale.
AI.motivation: To understand how star formation scales with cloud properties (mass, surface density, free-fall time) across a broad range of molecular cloud sizes and distances in the Milky Way, and to test whether canonical star formation scaling relations hold at the scale of individual molecular clouds.
AI.method: The authors assemble a sample of 45 molecular clouds (5-240 pc) spanning heliocentric distances of 1.1-14.4 kpc. Cloud masses are derived from 12CO and 13CO emission, stellar masses from the YSO population, and star formation efficiencies and rates computed. Scaling relations between SFR, cloud mass, SFE, surface densities, and free-fall time are examined statistically.
AI.result: Cloud masses range from ~10^3 to 2.3x10^6 M_sun with SFEs up to 0.33. A tight, nearly linear SFR-cloud mass scaling is found. SFE declines with cloud mass. The Sigma_SFR vs Sigma_gas relation shows large cloud-to-cloud scatter, indicating the Kennicutt-Schmidt law is not strongly recovered at individual cloud scales. SFE per free-fall time is not universal and decreases with increasing gas mass available per free-fall time.
AI.conclusion: Star formation scales approximately linearly with cloud mass, but the efficiency per cloud and per free-fall time varies systematically with cloud properties. The free-fall time plays an important regulatory role in star formation, though the SFE per free-fall time is not a universal constant, with implications for theoretical models of molecular cloud evolution and star formation.

title: Molecular absorption lines toward the Galactic ISM detected at 89 GHz with VLBI
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in PASJ
summary: As the first step to explore the Galactic foreground interstellar medium (ISM) with high angular resolution, we investigated the detectability of molecular absorption lines with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI). This paper reports our first observations of HCO+ J=1-0 and HCN J=1-0 molecular absorption lines toward four extragalactic compact radio sources with the Korean VLBI Network (KVN). HCO+ absorption lines were detected in all directions and HCN absorption lines in three directions. All of these detections, except for two HCO+ detections, are reported here for the first time with VLBI. We find that the column density ratio N(HCN)/N(HCO+) obtained with VLBI is consistent with the trend established from observations with connected-element interferometers, demonstrating the feasibility of future VLBI studies of molecular absorption.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first VLBI observations of HCO+ J=1-0 and HCN J=1-0 molecular absorption lines toward four extragalactic compact radio sources using the Korean VLBI Network (KVN). HCO+ absorption was detected in all four directions and HCN in three, with most detections being new to VLBI. The measured column density ratio N(HCN)/N(HCO+) is consistent with connected-element interferometer results, validating the feasibility of future VLBI studies of molecular absorption.
AI.motivation: To explore the Galactic foreground interstellar medium (ISM) with high angular resolution, which requires testing the detectability of molecular absorption lines using VLBI techniques.
AI.method: VLBI observations of HCO+ J=1-0 and HCN J=1-0 absorption lines toward four extragalactic compact radio sources using the Korean VLBI Network (KVN). Column density ratios were computed and compared with established trends from connected-element interferometer observations.
AI.result: HCO+ absorption lines were detected toward all four sources and HCN toward three. Most detections (except two HCO+) are reported for the first time with VLBI. The N(HCN)/N(HCO+) column density ratio agrees with the trend from connected-element interferometers.
AI.conclusion: VLBI observations of molecular absorption lines are feasible and reliable, enabling future high-angular-resolution studies of the Galactic foreground ISM.

title: AT 2022csn: A Photometrically Peculiar Optical/UV Tidal Disruption Event in a Type II AGN
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The emission mechanism and host galaxy preference of optical/UV tidal disruption events (TDEs) are still not entirely understood. We present observations of the TDE AT 2022csn, which is one of the most distant (d_L~726 Mpc) and luminous (L_peak=2.487^(+0.073)_(-0.067)*10^(44) erg/s) optical/UV TDEs observed to date. Although it is a spectroscopically normal H+He TDE, it shows some photometric peculiarities, exhibiting a pronounced double-peaked light curve (with peaks separated by 18.30 pm 2.84 days in the g-band), and lying in the low-temperature and large-radius end of the optical/UV TDE population. The host galaxy of AT 2022csn shows evidence for a significant starburst within the last ~Gyr consistent with other optical/UV TDEs, but also narrow emission lines that place it within the Type II AGN region of the BPT diagram. Interaction between the TDE and a pre-existing AGN accretion disk might explain the peculiar photometric properties. However, it is puzzling that a TDE would be visible in a Type II AGN, where according to the AGN unification picture the central region around the supermassive black hole is obscured. We suggest a few scenarios to reconcile this. AT 2022csn together with AT 2019ahk, which shows similar properties, may belong to a new subset of low-temperature, high-radius TDEs in galaxies with Type II AGN emission features.

AI.tldr: This paper presents observations of AT 2022csn, one of the most distant and luminous optical/UV tidal disruption events (TDEs) known, exhibiting a double-peaked light curve and lying at the low-temperature, large-radius end of the TDE population. Its host galaxy shows both a recent starburst and Type II AGN emission features, which is puzzling given the AGN unification picture. The authors propose TDE-AGN disk interaction scenarios and suggest AT 2022csn and AT 2019ahk may define a new subclass of TDEs in Type II AGN host galaxies.
AI.motivation: The emission mechanism and host galaxy preferences of optical/UV TDEs remain poorly understood. Studying extreme cases like AT 2022csn—one of the most distant and luminous TDEs observed—can provide crucial constraints on TDE physics, especially regarding interactions with pre-existing AGN accretion disks and the tension with the AGN unification paradigm.
AI.method: The authors present multi-wavelength photometric and spectroscopic observations of AT 2022csn (luminosity distance ~726 Mpc), analyzing its light curve morphology (revealing a double-peaked structure with peaks separated by ~18.3 days in the g-band), its spectral classification as a normal H+He TDE, and the host galaxy properties via emission-line diagnostics (placing it in the Type II AGN region of the BPT diagram) and evidence for a recent starburst within the last ~Gyr.
AI.result: AT 2022csn is a spectroscopically normal H+He TDE but photometrically peculiar, with a pronounced double-peaked light curve and low-temperature, high-radius properties. The host galaxy harbors both a recent starburst and Type II AGN signatures. Together with AT 2019ahk, these objects may represent a new subclass of low-temperature, high-radius TDEs hosted in galaxies with Type II AGN emission features. TDE-AGN disk interaction is proposed as a possible explanation for the peculiar photometry, though the visibility of a TDE in an obscured AGN is puzzling and several reconciliation scenarios are suggested.
AI.conclusion: AT 2022csn is an extreme example of the optical/UV TDE population in terms of distance and luminosity, and its peculiar double-peaked photometry suggests possible interaction with a pre-existing AGN accretion disk. The coexistence of a TDE with Type II AGN features challenges the AGN unification picture, prompting the authors to propose a new potential subclass of TDEs in Type II AGN host galaxies, with AT 2019ahk as a similar member.

title: Tracing luminous infrared galaxy populations through cluster evolution in a cosmological mock redshift survey
comment: 16 pages, 13 figures. Submitted to Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: We present GARDENS-Wide, a new 100 square degree mock redshift survey of the dusty star-forming galaxy population based on the MultiDark-Planck 2 dark-matter halo simulation. The mock reproduces observed multiwavelength number counts at 500 $μ$m, 1.1, 1.4 and 2.0 mm. The large simulated area enables us to identify gravitationally bound systems, trace their assembly histories, and quantify the redshift evolution of their galaxy content and structural extent. We find strong evolution in the fractional contribution of galaxy populations within cluster progenitors. Star-forming galaxies account for ~35 per cent of members at low redshift, increasing to 60-65 per cent at $z\sim2$ and declining to ~20 per cent by $z\sim5$. LIRGs contribute ~20-40 per cent, peaking near $z\sim2$, while ULIRGs remain subdominant and HyLIRGs are rare. We measure proto-cluster radii as the maximum 3D comoving distance from the central halo to the most distant member halo. Proto-clusters contract significantly over cosmic time, from >20 comoving Mpc at high redshift to a few Mpc at $z\sim0$. ULIRGs become increasingly centrally concentrated at $z>1.5$ in rich proto-clusters. We provide observational predictions for the TolTEC Large-Scale Structure survey.

AI.tldr: GARDENS-Wide is a new 100 sq-degree mock redshift survey of dusty star-forming galaxies built from the MultiDark-Planck 2 simulation. It reproduces observed multiwavelength number counts and reveals strong redshift evolution in galaxy populations within proto-clusters, significant proto-cluster contraction over cosmic time, and increasing central concentration of ULIRGs at high redshift.
AI.motivation: To understand the assembly history and structural evolution of dusty star-forming galaxies within gravitationally bound systems (proto-clusters), and to provide observational predictions for upcoming large-scale structure surveys like TolTEC.
AI.method: Using the MultiDark-Planck 2 dark-matter halo simulation to build a 100 sq-degree mock redshift survey of dusty star-forming galaxies, calibrating to observed multiwavelength number counts at 500 μm, 1.1, 1.4, and 2.0 mm. Gravitationally bound systems are identified to trace assembly histories, galaxy content, and structural extent (proto-cluster radii) as a function of redshift.
AI.result: Star-forming galaxies shift from ~35% of cluster members at low redshift to 60-65% at z~2 then decline to ~20% by z~5. LIRGs peak at ~20-40% near z~2; ULIRGs remain subdominant and HyLIRGs are rare. Proto-cluster radii contract from >20 comoving Mpc at high redshift to a few Mpc at z~0. ULIRGs become increasingly centrally concentrated at z>1.5 in rich proto-clusters.
AI.conclusion: The mock successfully reproduces observed number counts and provides quantitative predictions for the redshift evolution of galaxy populations and proto-cluster structure, offering specific observational expectations for the TolTEC Large-Scale Structure survey.

title: A "Neutrino Fog" For Gravitational Waves: The Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background from Supernova Neutrino Memory
comment: 20 pages, 9 figures, to be submitted to PRD. Comments welcome!
summary: Gravitational waves originating from unresolved sources, or stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWBs), carry precious information about the physics underlying their diverse sources, and represent an important target for future experimental searches. Here, we model the SGWB due to core collapse supernovae. Using an extensive collection of state-of-the-art, three-dimensional, multi-second supernova simulations, we characterize the two main components of this background: one at $f \sim 10^{-2} - 1$ Hz, due to anisotropic neutrino emission (the gravitational wave memory); the other at $f \gtrsim 10^{2}$ Hz, from the near-core matter dynamics. We find that the memory component offers the best prospects of detection, as its characteristic peak at $f\sim 0.1$ Hz is within the reach of future space-born detectors. At the peak, the energy density might be comparable to that of backgrounds from slow roll inflation and from possible cosmological relics, thus potentially impacting searches of these important signals.

AI.tldr: The paper models the stochastic gravitational wave background from core collapse supernovae using state-of-the-art 3D multi-second simulations, finding two main components: a neutrino-emission-driven memory component at ~0.01-1 Hz and a matter-dynamics component at >100 Hz. The memory component at ~0.1 Hz is detectable by future space-based detectors and may be comparable in energy density to inflationary or cosmological relic backgrounds.
AI.motivation: Stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWBs) from unresolved sources encode valuable information about their source physics and represent an important target for future experimental searches. Modeling the SGWB from core collapse supernovae is necessary to understand its properties and assess its impact on detecting other cosmological signals.
AI.method: The authors use an extensive collection of state-of-the-art, three-dimensional, multi-second core collapse supernova simulations to model the SGWB, characterizing two distinct frequency components: the gravitational wave memory component from anisotropic neutrino emission at ~0.01-1 Hz, and the near-core matter dynamics component at ~100 Hz.
AI.result: The memory component offers the best detection prospects, with its characteristic peak at ~0.1 Hz within reach of future space-based detectors. At the peak, the energy density may be comparable to backgrounds from slow roll inflation and possible cosmological relics.
AI.conclusion: The supernova SGWB memory component could significantly impact searches for inflationary and cosmological relic backgrounds, making it an important astrophysical foreground to account for in future space-based gravitational wave detector analyses.

title: PDRs4All XXII. Near-Infrared continuum in the Orion Bar
comment: 15 pages, 13 figures
summary: Conspicuous excess emission is present in the near-infrared (NIR) region in various objects, including reflection nebulae, planetary nebulae, and nearby galaxies. However, the spatial distribution and spectral shape of the excess emission remain poorly understood. We studied the NIR continuum emission spectroscopically and obtained its spatial distribution relative to the aromatic infrared band (AIB) at 3.3um in the Orion Bar prototypical photodissociation region (PDR). We aim to characterize its spectral shape and discuss its origin. We employed 3D spectroscopic data of the Orion Bar taken with the integrated field unit of NIRSpec on JWST from the Early Release Science program "PDRs4All." Contribution from the foreground ionized gas was estimated using the Cloudy code and subtracted. The observed regions were divided into nine physically distinct regions and an average spectrum was derived for each region. The nine regions, including the ionized gas, atomic PDR, and molecular PDR, clearly show remaining continuum in the region 1--4.5um. The continuum at wavelengths longer than 2.7um shows good correlations with the 3.3um AIB, while the correlation of the continuum at 1.2um is not significant. We further find that the NIR continuum in the Orion Bar can be approximated by a summation of two blackbodies. The low-temperature component correlates with the AIB well, while the high-temperature component does not. The average spectra also show absorption features at 3.0 and 4.27um, which are attributed to the presence in the spectra of water ice and CO2 ice. We discuss possible origins of the NIR continuum, among which recurrent fluorescence from carbon clusters better explains the observed low-temperature component. The presence of ice species suggests a contribution from a deeper layer of the PDR along the line of sight producing characteristic ice absorption features.

AI.tldr: This study uses JWST NIRSpec IFU 3D spectroscopic data of the Orion Bar PDR to characterize the spatial distribution and spectral shape of conspicuous NIR excess continuum emission (1–4.5 μm). The continuum is approximated by two blackbody components: a low-temperature component that correlates well with the 3.3 μm AIB and is attributed to recurrent fluorescence from carbon clusters, and a high-temperature component that does not correlate with the AIB. Absorption features at 3.0 and 4.27 μm indicate water ice and CO2 ice contributions from deeper PDR layers.
AI.motivation: The NIR continuum excess emission is observed in various astronomical objects (reflection nebulae, planetary nebulae, nearby galaxies) but its spatial distribution and spectral shape remain poorly understood. This work aims to characterize its spectral shape and origin using the Orion Bar as a prototypical PDR.
AI.method: Using 3D spectroscopic data from the JWST NIRSpec IFU (PDRs4All Early Release Science program), the authors subtract the foreground ionized gas contribution modeled with the Cloudy code. The observed regions are divided into nine physically distinct regions (ionized gas, atomic PDR, molecular PDR), and average spectra are derived for each. The continuum is fit with a two-blackbody model and correlations with the 3.3 μm AIB are examined.
AI.result: Residual NIR continuum (1–4.5 μm) is present in all nine regions. The continuum longward of 2.7 μm correlates strongly with the 3.3 μm AIB, while the 1.2 μm continuum shows no significant correlation. The continuum is well approximated by two blackbodies: a low-temperature component correlating with the AIB, and a high-temperature component that does not. Absorption features at 3.0 and 4.27 μm indicate water ice and CO2 ice, suggesting contributions from deeper PDR layers.
AI.conclusion: Recurrent fluorescence from carbon clusters is the most plausible origin for the low-temperature NIR continuum component correlated with the AIB. The ice absorption features imply line-of-sight contamination from deeper, colder PDR regions, providing new constraints on the origin and structure of NIR continuum emission in PDRs.

title: Gamma-ray and radio populations of millisecond pulsars in globular clusters
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to JHEAP
summary: The populations of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) across the Milky Way's globular cluster (GC) system serve as powerful diagnostics of neutron star evolution in a variety of dense stellar environments. Using properties of 118 Galactic GCs, we performed Monte Carlo simulations of their gamma-ray fluxes observed by Fermi. We compared two luminosity models: a 3D fundamental plane (model A) and a lognormal distribution (model B). Both models reproduce the observed gamma-ray fluxes and mirror the scaling law with the GC stellar encounter rate established for low-mass X-ray binaries and radio MSPs. Due to its lower average gamma-ray luminosities, model B predicts a 6-7 times larger MSP population ($5150^{+720}_{-710}$) than model A ($770\pm60$). Furthermore, both models accurately predict a population-wide expectation of roughly three clusters whose aggregate gamma-ray emission is dominated by a single bright MSP. Invoking a radio-to-gamma-ray luminosity scaling ($L_r \sim 3.5 \times 10^{-7} L_γ$), we find that model B predicts a mean radio pseudoluminosity ($\log L_{\rm pseudo} \sim -1.6$) that is fainter than canonical pulsars. This result is consistent with recent evidence attributing the apparent faintness of Galactic MSPs to geometric effects. In contrast, model A implies an intrinsically brighter population ($\log L_{\rm pseudo} \sim -0.3$) that lacks a clear physical basis and is inconsistent with the results found for Galactic pulsars. The larger underlying population of faint millisecond pulsars predicted by model B could be probed by sensitive surveys with emerging radio facilities to further constrain the evolutionary pathways of MSPs.

AI.tldr: The paper compares two luminosity models (a 3D fundamental plane and a lognormal distribution) for millisecond pulsars in Galactic globular clusters using Fermi gamma-ray observations of 118 clusters. The lognormal model (B) predicts a 6-7 times larger MSP population than the fundamental plane model (A), and is consistent with geometric explanations for the apparent faintness of Galactic MSPs, whereas model A implies an intrinsically brighter population lacking physical basis.
AI.motivation: To constrain the population size and evolutionary pathways of millisecond pulsars in globular clusters by evaluating which gamma-ray luminosity model is most physically consistent with both Fermi observations and radio pulsar properties.
AI.method: Monte Carlo simulations of gamma-ray fluxes from 118 Galactic globular clusters observed by Fermi, comparing a 3D fundamental plane luminosity model (A) against a lognormal distribution model (B), and invoking a radio-to-gamma-ray luminosity scaling to test consistency with radio pulsar pseudoluminosities.
AI.result: Both models reproduce observed gamma-ray fluxes and the encounter-rate scaling law, but model B predicts 5150 MSPs versus 770 for model A. Model B yields a mean radio pseudoluminosity (log ~ -1.6) fainter than canonical pulsars, consistent with geometric effects, while model A implies a brighter intrinsic population (log ~ -0.3) lacking physical basis.
AI.conclusion: The lognormal luminosity model (B) is favored as it predicts a larger underlying population of faint MSPs, consistent with geometric explanations for pulsar apparent faintness, and can be tested with sensitive surveys using emerging radio facilities.

title: The mass-dependent interplay of active galacitc nuclei and supernova feedback in shaping the $L_{\rm X}$--$T$ relation of early-type galaxies
comment: 14 pages, 8 figures, published in A&A
summary: The observed X-ray luminosity--temperature ($L_{\rm X}$--$T$) relation of hot gas in early-type galaxies deviates significantly from the prediction of purely gravitational heating, providing a key constraint on non-gravitational processes such as supernova (SN) and active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback. We investigate the physical origin of this relation using high-resolution 3D hydrodynamical simulations with the multiscale AGN-regulated cosmic ecosystem resolver in 3D (MACER3D) framework, which we applied to a dwarf elliptical, a massive elliptical, and a cluster-central galaxy. For comparison, we performed controlled simulations that included AGN winds and SN feedback in isolation, excluding cosmological inflow and environmental effects. The dominant regulation mechanism depends strongly on the halo mass. In the cluster-central case, neither AGN winds nor SN feedback alone can sufficiently suppress the gas density and $L_{\rm X}$. When both are included, their nonlinear coupling suppresses the X-ray emission, producing ($L_{\rm X}$, $T$) values below the observed relation; this discrepancy can be resolved by incorporating AGN jet feedback. In massive elliptical galaxies, the inclusion of AGN feedback brings the model predictions into broad agreement with the observed $L_{\rm X}$--$T$ relation, indicating that AGN feedback dominates SN feedback. At the low-mass end, dwarf galaxy models also follow the observed trend. In this regime, models with either SN or AGN feedback alone predict low $L_{\rm X}$. When both are included, AGN wind-driven transport of SN-enriched gas to intermediate radii enhances the metallicity and radiative cooling, thereby increasing $L_{\rm X}$. This coupled process establishes a fountain-like circulation, in which gas is repeatedly lifted and recycled within the galaxy.

AI.tldr: This paper uses high-resolution 3D hydrodynamical simulations (MACER3D) to investigate the physical origin of the observed X-ray luminosity-temperature (L_X–T) relation of hot gas in early-type galaxies. The dominant feedback mechanism regulating this relation depends strongly on halo mass: both AGN and SN feedback are needed (plus AGN jets) for cluster-central galaxies, AGN feedback dominates in massive ellipticals, and coupled SN+AGN feedback drives fountain-like circulation in dwarfs.
AI.motivation: The observed L_X–T relation of hot gas in early-type galaxies deviates significantly from purely gravitational heating predictions, providing a key constraint on non-gravitational processes such as SN and AGN feedback. Understanding the physical origin of this deviation is essential for constraining feedback models.
AI.method: High-resolution 3D hydrodynamical simulations using the MACER3D (multiscale AGN-regulated cosmic ecosystem resolver in 3D) framework, applied to three galaxy types: a dwarf elliptical, a massive elliptical, and a cluster-central galaxy. Controlled simulations isolating AGN winds and SN feedback were compared against runs including cosmological inflow and environmental effects.
AI.result: The dominant regulation mechanism depends strongly on halo mass. In cluster-centrals, neither AGN winds nor SN alone suffice, but their nonlinear coupling suppresses L_X below observed values, which is resolved by adding AGN jet feedback. In massive ellipticals, AGN feedback brings predictions into broad agreement with observation and dominates SN feedback. In dwarfs, combined SN+AGN feedback drives AGN wind transport of SN-enriched gas to intermediate radii, enhancing metallicity and cooling to increase L_X, establishing a fountain-like circulation.
AI.conclusion: The physical origin of the L_X–T relation in early-type galaxies is governed by mass-dependent feedback mechanisms: AGN jets are necessary to match observations in cluster-centrals, AGN feedback dominates in massive ellipticals, and a coupled SN+AGN fountain-like circulation operates in dwarf galaxies. The study demonstrates that the observed relation encodes the interplay of multiple feedback processes that vary with halo mass.

title: The Indian Pulsar Timing Array Data Release 2: III. Search for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background
summary: We present the first independent search for an isotropic stochastic gravitational wave background in the second data release of the Indian Pulsar Timing Array, comprising of 27 millisecond pulsars monitored simultaneously in two frequency bands with the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope over a maximum 7.2 year baseline. Building on a comprehensive single pulsar noise analysis, we search for a common uncorrelated red noise process within a Bayesian inference framework and with the noise-marginalized optimal statistics, and we test the robustness of the result through per-pulsar dropout analyses and solar-wind exclusion cuts. Leaving the spectral index free, we recover a broad amplitude posterior, $\log_{10} A_{\rm CURN} = -13.71^{+1.06}_{-3.28}$, with an unconstrained spectral index $γ_{\rm CURN} = 2.98^{+3.62}_{-2.70}$ and a Savage-Dickey Bayes factor of $2.5$ for a common red process over the no signal model. The optimal-statistic signal to noise ratios for the monopole, dipole, and Hellings-Downs correlations are all consistent with zero. Fixing the spectral index to $γ= 13/3$, the value predicted by an idealized toy model in which the background is sourced by a population of supermassive black hole binaries in circular orbits evolving purely under leading-order gravitational radiation reaction, we place a $95\%$ upper limit on the common-process amplitude of $A_{\rm GWB} < 3.4\times10^{-14}$, stable across solar elongation cuts of $10^\circ$, $20^\circ$, and $30^\circ$. title: Binary Constraints on the Origin of Nitrogen-rich Field Stars
summary: Recent JWST observations have revealed galaxies with unusually high N/O ratios, suggesting that nitrogen enrichment may be common in intense star-forming environments in the early Universe. In the Milky Way, nitrogen-rich(N-rich) stars in the Galactic field have long served as probes of early Galaxy formation and globular cluster enrichment. However, the identification of binaries among these stars raises the possibility that binary mass transfer could contribute to their origin. In this work, we utilize multi-epoch radial velocities and element abundances from APOGEE DR17 to constrain their formation sites. Among 266 N-rich field stars, 33 exhibit radial velocity variations of $Δ{\rm RV} > 1\,{\rm km/s}$, including 10 robust spectroscopic binaries identified using the $F_2$ statistic within a well-sampled subset of 46 stars. The resulting close-binary fraction ($21.7\pm6.1\%$) is statistically indistinguishable from that of chemically normal field stars ($18.1\pm0.6\%$), showing no evidence of the excess expected from AGB binary pollution. This is further supported by the absence of correlation between [N/Fe] and [Ce/Fe] and the lack of [C/Fe] enhancement. Crucially, we detect an anti-correlation between binary fraction and [Al/Fe], with strongly Al-enhanced stars ($[\mathrm{Al/Fe}] \gtrsim 0.5$) exhibiting a reduced binary fraction ($< 10\%$). This trend serves as a dynamical fingerprint of high-density environments, consistent with the efficient disruption of binaries via three-body interactions in GC cores. Our results do not support binary mass transfer as the dominant formation channel for N-rich field stars; they are predominantly GC escapees that retain the dynamical memory of their dense birth sites.

The close-binary fraction (21.7±6.1%) is indistinguishable from chemically normal stars, and an anti-correlation between binary fraction and [Al/Fe] supports a dynamical origin: N-rich field stars are predominantly GC escapees, not products of binary pollution.
AI.motivation: Recent JWST observations reveal galaxies with unusually high N/O ratios, prompting questions about nitrogen enrichment in early star-forming environments. In the Milky Way, N-rich field stars serve as probes of early galaxy formation and globular cluster enrichment, but the discovery of binaries among them raises uncertainty about whether binary mass transfer contributes to their origin.
AI.method: Multi-epoch radial velocities and elemental abundances from APOGEE DR17 are used to study 266 N-rich field stars. The F2 statistic identifies 10 robust spectroscopic binaries within a well-sampled subset of 46 stars. Binary fractions are compared to chemically normal field stars, and correlations between binary fraction, [N/Fe], [Ce/Fe], [C/Fe], and [Al/Fe] are examined.

Instead, they are predominantly globular cluster escapees whose reduced binary fraction among Al-enhanced stars reflects dynamical disruption via three-body interactions in dense GC cores, preserving the dynamical memory of their birth environments.

title: Structural quasi-universality in highly magnetized differentially rotating neutron stars
comment: 10 pages with 6 figures and 3 tables; comments welcome
summary: Universal relations among macroscopic properties of neutron stars provide a powerful framework to probe their internal structures while minimizing uncertainties associated with the equation of state (EoS). Although such relations have been extensively studied for uniformly rotating stars, their extension to differentially rotating and strongly magnetized configurations remains largely unexplored. We systematically investigate equilibrium configurations for a wide range of EoSs, rotation profiles, and magnetic field strengths. We establish a generalized quasi-universal relation between the moment of inertia and compactness that remains remarkably insensitive to the underlying EoS across uniformly rotating, differentially rotating, and strongly magnetized configurations. For sequences with fixed angular momentum, the normalized moment of inertia exhibits a quasi-universal dependence on compactness, with deviations primarily due to magnetic field strength and degree of differential rotation. We derive analytic expressions for these dependencies, enabling a unified phenomenological model applicable over a wide range of stellar configurations. As astrophysical applications, we quantify the systematic bias in magnetar luminosity estimates and the rotational kinetic energy of post-merger remnant of GW170817. These results extend quasi-universal relations beyond the standard assumptions of uniform rotation and weak magnetization, providing a robust framework for interpreting observations of highly magnetized and differentially rotating neutron stars, and enabling more reliable constraints on their astrophysical properties.

The authors derive analytic expressions for deviations due to magnetic field strength and differential rotation, and apply the framework to quantify systematic biases in magnetar luminosity estimates and the rotational kinetic energy of the GW170817 post-merger remnant.

Extending these relations is crucial for interpreting observations of highly magnetized and differentially rotating neutron stars, such as magnetars and post-merger remnants, while minimizing uncertainties from the equation of state.
AI.method: The authors systematically investigate equilibrium configurations across a wide range of EoSs, rotation profiles, and magnetic field strengths. They construct a generalized quasi-universal relation between the moment of inertia and compactness, and derive analytic expressions capturing the dependencies on magnetic field strength and the degree of differential rotation, enabling a unified phenomenological model.
AI.result: The generalized quasi-universal relation between moment of inertia and compactness is remarkably insensitive to the underlying EoS across all three configuration types. For fixed angular momentum sequences, the normalized moment of inertia shows quasi-universal dependence on compactness with deviations primarily controlled by magnetic field strength and differential rotation degree. The framework is applied to quantify systematic bias in magnetar luminosity estimates and rotational kinetic energy of the GW170817 post-merger remnant.

title: Chemical Abundances and Globular Clusters of Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies
comment: Proceedings of the IAU Symposium No. 403, The Hidden Beauty of Galactic Outskirts
summary: We present an overview of our ongoing GASTRONOMI project, which investigates the coevolution of the Milky Way (MW), its satellite dwarf galaxies, and their star clusters through chemo-dynamical analysis. We derive precise chemical abundances for stars in five classical dwarf galaxies, which reveal mass-dependent chemical evolution, particularly in alpha elements, such as [Si/Fe]. A distinct dichotomy in [Al/Fe] is found between metal-rich ([Fe/H]>-1.5) stars formed in-situ in the MW and those originating in dwarf galaxies. Star clusters act as sensitive environmental probes. The presence of multiple populations correlates with galactic evolution, and nitrogen-rich stars in Fornax are likely relics of disrupted globular clusters (GCs). We developed a chemical classification for Galactic GCs, isolating primordial populations by their low [Al/Fe]. This places in-situ and accreted GCs in distinct regions of the [Al/Fe]-[Fe/H] plane, providing a new tool to reconstruct the Galaxy's accretion history.

AI.tldr: The GASTRONOMI project investigates the coevolution of the Milky Way, its dwarf satellite galaxies, and their star clusters via chemo-dynamical analysis. It reveals mass-dependent chemical evolution in dwarf galaxies (e.g., [Si/Fe]), a clear [Al/Fe] dichotomy between in-situ MW stars and those from dwarf galaxies, and uses star clusters as environmental probes. A chemical classification for Galactic globular clusters based on [Al/Fe] separates in-situ from accreted clusters, offering a new tool for reconstructing the Galaxy's accretion history.
AI.motivation: To understand the coevolution of the Milky Way, its satellite dwarf galaxies, and their star clusters, and to reconstruct the Galaxy's assembly and accretion history through chemo-dynamical chemistry.
AI.method: Derivation of precise chemical abundances (e.g., [Si/Fe], [Al/Fe], [Fe/H]) for stars in five classical dwarf galaxies, combined with chemical classification of Galactic globular clusters based on their [Al/Fe] and [Fe/H] abundances, along with analysis of multiple populations and nitrogen-rich stars as tracers of disrupted clusters.

Nitrogen-rich stars in Fornax suggest relics of disrupted globular clusters. Chemical classification of GCs places in-situ and accreted clusters in distinct regions of the [Al/Fe]-[Fe/H] plane.
AI.conclusion: Chemical abundances, especially [Al/Fe] and [Fe/H], provide a powerful diagnostic to distinguish in-situ versus accreted stellar populations and star clusters, offering a new tool to reconstruct the Milky Way's accretion history and understand coevolution with its satellites.

title: EP241113a: dissipative photospheric emission from a dirty fireball
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures; published in ApJL
summary: EP241113a, a soft X-ray transient detected by the Einstein Probe (EP), has an isotropic-equivalent energy ($E_{γ,\rm{iso}}\sim 10^{51}{\, \rm erg}$) comparable to classical gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) but an exceptionally low peak energy ($E_{\rm{p}} \lesssim 1 \, {\rm keV}$), placing it off the canonical $E_{\rm{p}}$--$E_{γ,\rm{iso}}$ (Amati) relation at $>3σ$ confidence. The afterglow of EP241113a is also unusual, with an extremely low plateau luminosity and no jet break up to the latest observation. Such properties have been interpreted as arising from an energetic ``dirty fireball,'' i.e., a relativistic jet with energy comparable to classical GRBs but much higher baryon loading, leading to a bulk Lorentz factor of $Γ\sim 20$. In this {\it Letter}, we propose that low $E_{\rm{p}}$ arises from dissipative photospheric emission in such a low-$Γ$ jet. As $Γ$ decreases, the photosphere shifts outward while the internal shock radius moves inward, causing dissipation to occur well below the photosphere and making the prompt emission photosphere-dominated. Meanwhile, the thermalization radius also moves outward, reducing the comoving radiation temperature where the spectral peak is established. Combined with weaker Lorentz boosting, these effects naturally shift the observed $E_{\rm{p}}$ into the soft X-ray band. We further suggest that such a low-$Γ$ jet may be powered by neutrino--antineutrino ($ν\barν$) annihilation in a hyperaccreting disk formed during the core collapse of a massive star. Compared with the Blandford--Znajek process, neutrino annihilation can produce a dirtier jet through baryon entrainment from a neutrino-driven wind. EP241113a-like events therefore offer new insight into the dissipation physics and launching mechanisms of jets from collapsing massive stars.

The authors propose that its low E_p arises from dissipative photospheric emission in an energetic "dirty fireball" jet with low bulk Lorentz factor (Γ~20), where photosphere-dominated prompt emission and reduced comoving temperature shift the peak into soft X-rays. They further suggest this jet may be powered by νν̄ annihilation in a hyperaccreting disk, offering new insight into jet dissipation and launching mechanisms in collapsing massive stars.
AI.motivation: EP241113a exhibits unusual properties—soft X-ray prompt emission off the Amati relation and an anomalous afterglow—that challenge standard GRB jet models. The authors aim to explain these extreme observations within a physical framework and to identify the jet launching mechanism responsible for such a "dirty fireball."

AI.conclusion: EP241113a-like events provide a new window into both the dissipation physics (photosphere-dominated emission in low-Γ jets) and the launching mechanisms (νν̄ annihilation vs. Blandford–Znajek) of relativistic jets from collapsing massive stars, linking extreme soft-spectrum transients to classical GRBs within a unified framework.

title: MIGHTEE-HI / LADUMA: Investigating the link between baryons and dynamics with 130 resolved HI-selected galaxies
comment: 21 pages, 18 figures
summary:
The baryonic Tully-Fisher relation (bTFR) and the radial acceleration relation (RAR) link the observed dynamics in galaxies to that expected from their baryonic mass distributions. The relations' small intrinsic scatters place strong constraints on galaxy formation models, dark matter properties and theories of modified dynamics, yet detailed measurements beyond the very local Universe remain limited. We use 130 purely HI-selected galaxies with resolved HI kinematics and baryonic mass profiles to measure the bTFR and RAR up to $z\approx0.09$.
  We measure a tight RAR with an acceleration scale $a_0=(1.50\pm0.05)\times10^{-10},{\rm m,s^{-2}}$ and an intrinsic scatter of $0.096\pm0.006$ dex, consistent with local results. We fit the bTFR in the `inverse' direction, conditioning on $M_{\rm bar}$ to mitigate HI flux-related selection effects, measuring a logarithmic slope of $0.27\pm0.01$ (corresponding to a forward slope of $3.72\pm0.16$), with vertical intrinsic scatter $σ_\perp\approx0.05$ dex. Fitting the general $δ$-family of MOND interpolating functions to the RAR, we infer $δ=4.10^{+1.4}_{-0.68}$, consistent with the value required by Solar System gravitational constraints and a null Wide Binary Test. We find no significant redshift evolution in the RAR acceleration scale for our pure HI-selected sample. However, the bTFR zero-point shows an apparent evolutionary trend that is strongly dependent on the fit direction: the traditional forward fit yields an $8.7σ$ preference for $z$ evolution, while for our fiducial inverse fit, this reduces to $3.4σ$, within $\approx2σ$ of the RAR evolution constraint. This suggests selection effects bias the forward fit; a careful consideration of such effects will be required in future endeavours to robustly measure the redshift evolution of dynamical scaling relations.

This work aims to extend these measurements to higher redshifts.
AI.method: The authors use 130 purely HI-selected galaxies with resolved HI kinematics and baryonic mass profiles to measure the bTFR and RAR up to z≈0.09. No significant redshift evolution is found in the RAR, but the bTFR zero-point evolution depends strongly on fit direction: 8.7σ for forward vs 3.4σ for inverse fit.

title: One year of broadband radio monitoring of the enigmatic transient GRB 250702B reveals the evolution of the relativistic jet
comment: 29 pages, 15 figures, submitted to MNRAS. All data in Table D1 available in machine readable format upon request. Comments welcome
summary: We present an extensive radio monitoring campaign of the unique extragalactic transient GRB 250702B, with observations spanning 0.65-233 GHz from 6-356 d (observer frame) post-discovery. The radio emission shows a smoothly evolving peaked synchrotron spectrum consistent with an adiabatic shock expanding into a stratified ambient medium ($n_e\propto R^{-k}$; $k= 1.5-2$). We detect significant variability in the low frequency ($\leq3$ GHz) light curves which we interpret as interstellar scintillation, placing an approximate bound on the blast wave image size of $1.2\times10^{16}\lesssim R_{\perp} \lesssim 5\times10^{17}$ cm. The temporal evolution of the flux density and critical synchrotron frequencies suggest the shock that powers the radio emission is potentially a wide-angle $θ_j\gtrsim15$ deg, low Lorentz factor ($Γ\lesssim10$) jet, or a narrow $θ_j\lesssim2$ deg highly relativistic jet. A narrow jet is expected for a stellar-mass black hole engine, such as a helium star merger, and the beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is consistent with the known distribution for long GRBs ($E_K\sim10^{51}$ erg). The wide-angle jet scenario would instead require a progenitor involving prolonged accretion. We derive and show an intermediate or stellar-mass black hole tidal disruption event are viable possibilities. The beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is on the low end of the known distribution for relativistic SMBH TDEs ($E_K\sim10^{50}$ erg). We disfavour an SMBH TDE due to lack of compatibility with the observed timescales. The detection of a jet shut off within the next year would favour a WD-IMBH TDE due to the shorter theoretical duration of super-Eddington accretion than the main-sequence TDE channels.

The authors find the progenitor could be either a wide-angle low-Lorentz-factor jet or a narrow highly relativistic jet, and consider intermediate-mass or stellar-mass black hole tidal disruption event (TDE) scenarios as viable, disfavoring an SMBH TDE based on timescales.

They fit the radio spectral energy distribution with a synchrotron model from an adiabatic shock in a stratified medium, analyzed low-frequency variability attributed to interstellar scintillation to bound the image size, tracked the temporal evolution of flux density and critical synchrotron frequencies, and compared the resulting jet parameters and kinetic energies to known distributions for long GRBs and relativistic TDEs.

title: Circumgalactic medium depletion drives satellite quenching in IllustrisTNG
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, plus appendices. Submitted to A&A. Comments are welcome!
summary: Satellite galaxies dominate the quenched population at low stellar masses ($M_\star \lesssim 10^{10}~\rm M_\odot$), yet identifying which processes shut down their star formation, their relative importance, and on what timescales, remains a central problem in galaxy evolution. We use MaNGA-like mock galaxies from IllustrisTNG to dissect different satellite quenching pathways, paying special attention to the role of the circumgalactic medium (CGM) during quenching phase. We reconstruct the baryonic, dark matter, structural, and chemical histories of $\sim$7 300 galaxies (2 800 satellites), using time since infall as the physical axis along which quenching unfolds. Satellites retain rotation-supported stellar kinematics throughout quenching, with disturbed velocity fields confined to systems with $M_\star \lesssim 10^{10.5}~\rm M_\odot$. For the first time, we present the coupled time evolution of the depletion of both the hot and cool gas reservoirs after infall: satellites lose $\sim$90% of their hot CGM within $\sim$$4.2^{+0.6}_{-0.6}$ Gyr, increasing with residence time and independent of stellar mass. The hot gas mass correlates strongly with SFR, establishing the CGM as the long-term fuel reservoir, unlike quenched centrals, which retain massive hot halos likely maintained by AGN feedback. Present-day quenched satellites were accreted earlier than star-forming ones (6.5$^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ vs. 4.3$^{+0.3}_{-0.3}$ Gyr ago), forming stars for at least $\sim$3 Gyr after infall before declining sharply, consistent with a delayed-then-rapid quenching scenario. Losing little stellar mass, yet with their gas depleted and their dark matter and metal-poor stellar outskirts tidally stripped, satellites emerge more compact and metal-rich than centrals at fixed mass. Our results suggest the gradual erosion of the hot CGM as the key link connecting infall to the slow shutdown of star formation.

AI.tldr: Using IllustrisTNG mock galaxies resembling MaNGA observations, the authors dissect satellite quenching pathways, showing that hot CGM depletion (~90% within 4.2 Gyr) correlates with star formation shutdown, supporting a delayed-then-rapid quenching scenario where satellites form stars for ~3 Gyr after infall before declining.
AI.motivation: Satellite galaxies dominate the quenched population at low stellar masses (M* ≲ 10^10 M_sun), but the specific processes, their relative importance, and the timescales over which they shut down star formation remain poorly understood.
AI.method: Analysis of ~7,300 MaNGA-like mock galaxies (2,800 satellites) from IllustrisTNG, reconstructing baryonic, dark matter, structural, and chemical histories using time since infall as the physical axis, and examining coupled evolution of hot and cool gas reservoirs alongside stellar kinematics and chemodynamical properties.
AI.result: Satellites retain rotation-supported kinematics throughout quenching, lose ~90% of hot CGM within ~4.2 Gyr (independent of stellar mass), show strong hot-gas-to-SFR correlation, were accreted earlier (6.5 vs 4.3 Gyr ago) than star-forming ones, and form stars for ~3 Gyr post-infall before a sharp decline. They emerge more compact and metal-rich than centrals at fixed mass due to tidal stripping of dark matter and metal-poor outskirts.
AI.conclusion: The gradual erosion of the hot CGM after infall is the key physical link connecting infall to the slow shutdown of star formation in satellites, distinct from quenched centrals whose hot halos are retained, likely via AGN feedback.

title: A JWST redshift for the host galaxy of EP250207b of z=3.2: a collapsar origin is viable

summary: We present James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and Hubble Space Telescope (HST) observations of the field of the fast X-ray transient (FXT) detected by Einstein Probe, EP250207b, to resolve any ambiguity about the host galaxy and redshift of the FXT. We model the X-ray, optical, near-infrared and radio light curves using a tophat jet model implemented in Redback and find that they are consistent with an on-axis gamma ray burst afterglow. The energetics and host galaxy properties do not allow us to distinguish between a collapsar and a merger driven event.

Multi-wavelength modeling with a tophat jet suggests an on-axis GRB afterglow, but the progenitor (collapsar vs. merger) remains ambiguous.

title: Profile Analysis of the Multiwavelength 2.1-year Oscillations of PG 1553+113

summary:
We investigate the morphology of the oscillation profiles of the blazar PG~1553+113 in relation to its well-known $\sim$2.1 yr periodicity. We identify individual cycles in the $γ$-ray, X-ray, UV, and optical light curves and characterize their temporal profiles using analytical models for single- and multi-peaked events.
  We find that the oscillations are generally described by a broad activity envelope with shorter-timescale substructure, showing that the $\sim$2.1 yr signal is not a strictly sinusoidal or self-similar modulation. The internal morphology varies across cycles and energy bands. This is particularly evident in X-rays, where all analyzed cycles show a strong formal preference for multi-component profiles, unlike the $γ$-ray band, where several cycles admit statistically comparable empirical descriptions.
  The contemporaneous MWL oscillations show broadly aligned activity episodes, but the timing and relative amplitudes of secondary components are not systematically repeated. This suggests that a common long-term modulation affects the broadband emission, while additional local or energy-dependent processes shape individual cycles. Such a picture is compatible with a geometric, jet-related contribution to the broad recurrent envelope, with intrinsic variability superimposed on it.
  We also identify new cycles with a dominant peak accompanied by weaker twin-peak-like features, similar to structures previously discussed in a supermassive black hole binary scenario for PG~1553+113. Although our results do not provide definitive evidence for this interpretation, the recurrence of comparable morphologies in newly analyzed cycles keeps this scenario viable.

While contemporaneous multi-wavelength oscillations show broadly aligned activity episodes, the timing and amplitudes of secondary components vary across cycles and energy bands, suggesting a common long-term modulation (possibly geometric/jet-related) with superimposed intrinsic variability. Some newly identified cycles show twin-peak-like features similar to those predicted in a supermassive black hole binary scenario, keeping that interpretation viable.
AI.motivation: To characterize the temporal morphology of the recurring ~2.1 yr oscillations in PG 1553+113 across multiple energy bands, determine whether the modulation is strictly sinusoidal or more complex, and assess whether observed structures support the supermassive black hole binary scenario.
AI.method: Individual oscillation cycles are identified in γ-ray, X-ray, UV, and optical light curves, and their temporal profiles are fitted using analytical models for single- and multi-peaked events, allowing a quantitative comparison of cycle morphology within and across energy bands.
AI.result: The oscillations are broad activity envelopes with shorter-timescale substructure rather than sinusoidal or self-similar modulations. X-ray cycles consistently prefer multi-component profiles, while γ-ray cycles often admit comparable single/multi-peak descriptions. Multi-wavelength oscillations show broadly aligned episodes but non-repeating secondary component timing and amplitudes, indicating a common long-term modulation with superimposed local or energy-dependent variability. New cycles with dominant peaks plus weaker twin-peak features are identified, resembling structures from the SMBH binary scenario.
AI.conclusion: The broadband recurrent ~2.1 yr modulation likely has a geometric/jet-related origin, while individual cycles are shaped by additional intrinsic or energy-dependent processes. The recurring twin-peak morphologies in newly analyzed cycles keep the supermassive black hole binary scenario viable, though definitive evidence is not provided.

title: General-relativistic structure of two-component quantum dark fermion stars
comment: 19 pages, 10 figures and 3 tables. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D
summary: We develop a general-relativistic framework for two-component quantum dark fermion stars: equilibrium configurations of two degenerate fermion species governed by gravity, a Yukawa-mediated dark fifth force and a globally relevant Bohm quantum-pressure correction. The treatment retains the full covariant form of the nonlinear Klein--Gordon equation in the Schwarzschild interior, with closure relations valid at arbitrary compactness, from the ultralight baseline up to densities of order $0.16\,\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$ at which relativistic scalar densities and self-consistent effective fermion masses become unavoidable. Two Lagrangian parameters, the dark-fermion mass and the dimensionless ratio between the Yukawa channel and gravity, together fix the equilibrium structure; a joint measurement of mass and radius therefore constrains the dark-sector microphysics directly from gravitational-wave observables. For particle masses in the band $10^{-11}$--$10^{-10}$ eV, the configurations exhibit radii of $3$--$24\,\mathrm{km}$ and compactness in the range $0.14$--$0.34$, behaving as dual mimickers: at moderate compactness they overlap with neutron stars in mass, radius, and inspiral frequency; at the most compact end ($κ\sim 0.34$, $R_T/R_S\simeq 1.5$) they cross the photon sphere and could masquerade as low-mass black holes in the mass-gap region. Tidal-deformability measurements discriminate against both populations: the dimensionless tidal deformability is measurably smaller than the neutron-star value yet remains non-zero, unlike that of a genuine black hole. These objects populate the sensitivity bands of LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer, producing astrometric microlensing signatures individually resolvable by \textit{Gaia}. The framework thus provides a reproducible and falsifiable template for constraining dark-sector properties through multi-messenger observations.

The full covariant nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation is retained in the Schwarzschild interior with closure relations valid at arbitrary compactness. Two Lagrangian parameters (dark-fermion mass and Yukawa-to-gravity ratio) fix the equilibrium structure. For masses 10^-11–10^-10 eV, configurations have radii 3–24 km and compactness 0.14–0.34, mimicking neutron stars at moderate compactness and low-mass black holes at the most compact end. Tidal deformability measurements can discriminate these objects from both, and they populate LISA, Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer sensitivity bands with Gaia-resolvable microlensing signatures.
AI.motivation: To provide a reproducible and falsifiable theoretical framework for constraining dark-sector microphysics via astrophysical gravitational-wave and multi-messenger observables, enabling dark matter configurations to be distinguished from neutron stars and black holes.
AI.method: General-relativistic framework for two-component degenerate fermion dark stars, incorporating gravity, a Yukawa-mediated dark fifth force, and a globally relevant Bohm quantum-pressure correction. The treatment retains the full covariant nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation in the Schwarzschild interior with closure relations valid at arbitrary compactness, including relativistic scalar densities and self-consistent effective fermion masses at high densities.
